## Session context dump — T282 (wrapper follow-ups) What I read: AGENTS.md (via project context), docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md, docs/infra/fleet-git-isolation.md (T278's rulings), the brief untracked/T282-wrapper-followups.md, tools/git-commit-mine, tools/regression-git-commit-mine.sh, tools/hooks/pre-commit, tools/regression-precommit.sh, docs/infra/agents/findings-schema.json, findings/README.md, docs/status/CURRENT.md. ### What I concluded, and on what evidence 1. **Defect 1 reproduced exactly as briefed** (scratch repo, /tmp/weizigo/t282-repro): mixed invocation (docs/new.md + already-committed docs/old.md) committed new.md correctly then printed `FAIL — commit does not contain: docs/old.md`, RC=1. Pure already-committed invocation exited 2 "REFUSED — nothing staged". Both are false alarms on healthy states. Fix = three-case verify-after + clean no-op at the empty-staged check. Evidence: the two regression arms (6, 7) plus the repro. 2. **Case-2 detection primitive** verified empirically: `git diff --quiet HEAD --

` alone returns 0 for a nonexistent path, so `git cat-file -e HEAD:

` must guard it. Also verified `git show --name-only` lists deleted paths (deletion commits pass case 1). 3. **The hook could not be a second copy of the scope parsing** — that is the drift mechanism that ends with the hook refusing the wrapper's own commits. Extracted tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh, shared by both; wrapper behavior in T278's five arms is unchanged (all still PASS). 4. **Rulings on the hook's identity question**, per the brief's steer, made explicit: absent identity → warn-and-allow listing paths (refusing would wedge the Orchestrator); unresolvable identity → warn-and-allow (identity unknown = unlabelled); wrapper --explicit → warn-and-allow via a new GIT_MINE_EXPLICIT=1 channel (without it, the hook would refuse the Orchestrator's sanctioned explicit-mode commits with foreign staged content — the exact seat that caused incident 2). Only identity-known + out-of-scope staged → REFUSE. 5. **T278's task-identity mode was never tested** — its regression only exercised --bundle. The pre-commit backstop now depends on that kanban path, so I added arms 8/9 covering it (pass). ### What I could not establish - A seeded control for verify-after case 3 (genuine missing): unreachable through the wrapper's own flow (git add fails first for missing/ignored paths; any staged path lands in the commit). It is a race safety net; stated honestly in the findings, no fake control invented. - Whether the live pre-commit hook will behave identically on macOS /bin/sh vs the bash run used in tests — the hook is POSIX sh and the scratch tests ran it via its own shebang; the end-to-end test used a real `git commit` in a scratch repo, which is the same invocation git uses in the live repo. ### Assumed without checking - MANAGENT_TASK_ID is unset in my own session (verified: it is) — the brief's unlabelled path applies to my own commits, and the wrapper's --task flag carries my identity. - The live kanban (docs/infra/managent/tasks.json) correctly resolves T282's bundle — verified via the lib CLI (task-bundle + scope both resolve T282 to untracked/T282-wrapper-followups.md and its deliverables). - claimlint's current counts are at floor (CURRENT.md T284 block) — regression-precommit.sh's null control passing confirms the hook's claimlint gate is not exceeded. ### Noticed but did not act on - **A worker can dodge both gates with `--explicit`** (it already skipped the wrapper's scope check; the hook matching that design is consistent). Closing it is a policy call for the Orchestrator (escape-hatch-free redesign), flagged in the findings. - The wrapper's empty-staged no-op (exit 0) is a new exit-code contract: scripts chaining the wrapper should treat RC=0 + "nothing to commit" as success. No caller chains it today (managent done asks git directly). - The hook now runs a python3 subprocess (via the lib) per identity-known commit; negligible cost, but it is the first python dependency inside the commit path (the wrapper already had one). - The live repo had unstaged foreign modifications (docs/infra/managent/*, src/managent/main.zig) throughout this session — the kanban's own writes and (possibly) another console's WIP. I never staged or committed them; the wrapper's foreign check only sees the index, which stayed clean apart from my own named paths. ### What I would check next - An independent seat re-running both regressions (verify-then-promote) before the backstop is called "working" — the QA-023 rules: trace one commit end-to-end through the hook, and confirm the wrapper's own identity-mode commit passes the hook in the live repo (it did once via the end-to-end scratch test, but the live repo's claimlint gate adds its own layer). - Whether `zig build test` (which wires in regression-precommit.sh) still passes with the modified hook — I ran regression-precommit.sh directly; the build integration was not re-run.
